dervis-irab:1-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النَّجْمِ) Well known; its plural is «نجوم», «أنجم», «أنجام» and «نُجُم». It is the star, and when used without qualification it means the Pleiades. As to what is meant by it here there are several views, among them that what is meant is the group of stars when they «هوت», i.e. fall and set from sight, and that the genus is intended. Al-Rāʿī said:
وبات يعدّ النجم في مستحيرة ... سريع بأيدي الآكلين جمودها
(He spent the night counting the stars in a pool of fat whose congealing was quick in the hands of those eating.)
It is also said that the Pleiades are meant, and that He swore by it when it falls and sets with the dawn; the Arabs apply the name «النجم» to the Pleiades in particular. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
فوردن والعيوق مقعد رائي ... الضرباء فوق النجم لا يتتلع
(They came to water while al-ʿAyyūq sat, as one who watches the drinkers, above the Pleiades, not rising.)
Ibn Durayd said: the Pleiades are seven stars, six visible and one hidden, with which people test their eyesight. It is also said that Allah swore by the Qur'an when He sent it down in scattered portions («نجوما») to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over twenty-three years.
(هَوى) Set («غرب»). Originally it means to fall from a height. Al-Rāghib said: "«الهوى» is falling from a height."
(مِرَّةٍ) Strength and force, or soundness in his intellect and opinion and firmness in his religion. The original sense of «المرّة» is the tightness of twisting. In the lexicons: «المرّة» is twisting; one says "a rope of strong «مرّة»"; it is also the state in which a thing continues, a strand of rope, strength and firmness of constitution, soundness of intellect, and one of the humours of the body, namely yellow bile and black bile.
(قابَ قَوْسَيْنِ) «القاب», «القيب», «القاد» and «القيد» mean the measure. Al-Zajjāj said:
"The Arabs were addressed according to their own language and the measure of their understanding; they were told about this what is said to one who delimits something. So the meaning is: it was, by what you would estimate, the measure of two bows or less than that." Ibn al-Sikkīt said: "«قاس الشيء يقوسه قوسا» is a dialectal variant of «قاسه يقيسه» when he measured it; and they have used for measurement the bow, the spear, the whip, the cubit, the fathom, the stride, the span, the «فتر» and the finger." In al-Qurṭubī: "«القاب» is what lies between the grip and the «سِيَة»; every bow has two «قاب»s. Some said, regarding His words «فكان قاب قوسين», that He meant «قابي قوس» (the two «قاب»s of a bow) and transposed it." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "The «سِيَة» of the bow is with a light «ياء», its «لام» being omitted; in relational form it returns, so one says «سيوي»; the «هاء» is a compensation for it. It is its curved tip. Abū ʿUbayda said: Ruʾba used to pronounce it with hamza, while the Arabs do not pronounce it with hamza. The upper «سِيَة» is called its hand and the lower its foot."

* I'rab:
(وَالنَّجْمِ إِذا هَوى) The «واو» is for oath; «النجم» is genitive by the «واو»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» ("I swear"); «إذا» is an adverbial for what is yet to come of time, and the operator in this adverbial is the omitted oath verb, i.e. "I swear by the star at the time of its falling". It is also said that «النجم» is the sending down of the Qur'an, in which case the operator in the adverbial would be «النجم» itself, though this i'rab is objected to, even if we prefer it. What follows is what al-Samīn [al-Ḥalabī] reported, which we quote verbatim because of its worth: "Regarding the operator in this adverbial there are several views, and each has a difficulty. One view is that it is accusative through the omitted oath verb, the implied form being «أقسم بالنجم وقت هويه»; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ and others, and it is problematic, for the oath verb is an inshāʾ (performative) and the inshāʾ is of the present, whereas «إذا» is for what is yet to come of time, so how can the two meet?
The second is that the operator in it is implied, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «النجم», i.e. "I swear by it while it is settled in the time of its falling"; and this is problematic on two counts. One is that «النجم» is a body («جثة») and time cannot be a ḥāl of a body, just as it cannot be a khabar; the other is that «إذا» is for the future, so how can it be a ḥāl? The first has been answered by saying that what is meant by «النجم» is a portion of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an was sent down in portions over twenty years; this is the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās and others. The second has been answered by saying it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). The third is that the operator in it is «النجم» itself when the Qur'an is meant by it; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ, and there is a flaw in it, because the Qur'an does not operate on the adverbial if it is meant as the name of this particular Book. It might be said that «النجم» has the sense of «المنجَّم» (the revealed in portions), as if it were said: "by the Qur'an revealed in portions at this time." This discussion occurs in several places, among them «والشمس وضحاها» and what follows it, and among them His words: «والليل إذا يغشى», and among them «والضحى والليل إذا سجى». A more specific discussion of this than this will come in [Sūrat] «والشمس», which you will find, if Allah wills." As for Abū Ḥayyān, he chose the ḥāl reading. He said: "«إذا» is an adverbial of time, and the operator in it is omitted, its implied form being «كائنا إذا هوى», and «كائنا» is accusative as a ḥāl: He, the Exalted, swore by the star in the state of its falling." The clause «هوى» is in the position of the genitive through the adverbial's being annexed to it.
(ما ضَلَّ صاحِبُكُمْ وَما غَوى) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the jawāb al-qasam (answer to the oath). He expressed it by "companionship" («الصحبة») because it better indicates intention, encouraging them toward him, turning them to him, and making hateful accusing him in his warning, given their knowledge of the purity of his character. «ضلّ صاحبكم» is a verb and agent; «وما غوى» is conjoined to «ما ضلّ».
(وَما يَنْطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوى) The «واو» is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «ينطق» is an imperfect verb and its agent is «هو» (he); «عن الهوى» is attached to «ينطق», i.e. "his speech does not proceed from a desire in himself", so «عن» is for transgression (departure), in its usual sense. It is also said that it has the sense of «الباء», so it would be attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحى) «إن» is negative; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «وحي» is the khabar of «هو»; and the clause «يوحى» is an adjective of «وحي».
(عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوى) The clause is a second adjective of «وحي». «علّمه» is a verb and direct object; «شديد القوى» is the agent of «علّمه», and what is meant by it is Jibrīl.
(ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوى) «ذو مرة» is an adjective of «شديد القوى»; the «فاء» is a conjunction; «استوى» is a verb and an implied agent.
(وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلى) The «واو» is circumstantial; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «بالأفق» is the khabar; «الأعلى» is an adjective of «الأفق»; and the clause is in the position of ḥāl.
(ثُمَّ دَنا فَتَدَلَّى) «ثم» is a conjunction of delay; «دنا» is a verb and its agent is implied, its implied form being «هو», i.e. Jibrīl; «فتدلى» is conjoined to «دنا». «التدلّي» is extension from above to below, and from «التدلي» the «دوالي» (vine branches) are derived, which carry the hanging grapes.
(فَكانَ قابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنى) The «فاء» is a conjunction; «كان» and its latent noun; «قاب قوسين» is its khabar. The sense of the sentence is: "so the measure of the distance of his nearness was like the «قاب» of two bows." There is an omission here of three muḍāfs, i.e. "so the measure of the distance of his nearness was like the measure of the «قاب» of two bows"; so three were omitted from the noun of «كان» and one from its khabar. «أو» is a conjunction, «أو» of permissibility; «أدنى» is conjoined to «قاب». This verse is like His words «أو يزيدون», and what was said about «أو» has already preceded. The meaning is: it was one of these two measures in the opinion of the observer; that is, because of the closeness of the two, the observer doubts about it. «أدنى» is a comparative (ism tafḍīl) and the thing compared with is omitted, its implied form being «أو أدنى من قاب قوسين»; or else «أو» has the sense of «بل», i.e. "rather nearer".
(فَأَوْحى إِلى عَبْدِهِ ما أَوْحى)
The «فاء» is a conjunction referring back to «علّمه شديد القوى». «أوحى» is a verb with an implied agent; «إلى عبده» is attached to «أوحى»; «ما» is relative or maṣdar, and in either case it, together with what follows it, is in the position of the accusative, as a direct object on the first view or an absolute object on the second. More discussion of it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(ما كَذَبَ الْفُؤادُ ما رَأى) «ما» is negative; «كذب الفؤاد» is a verb and agent. It was also read «كَذَّبَ» with shadda. «ما» is a relative noun, a direct object, since «كذب» is a verb that takes an object. Al-Akhṭal said:
كذبتك عينك أم رأيت بواسط ... غلس الظلام من ارباب خيالا
(Did your eye deceive you, or did you see at Wāsiṭ, in the dimness of the darkness, a phantom from al-Rabāb?)
It is also said that it does not take an object, so the accusative of «ما» would be by removal of the preposition, i.e. «فيما رآه». The author of al-Munjid claimed that «كذب» sometimes takes two objects; he said: "It sometimes takes two objects, so one says «كذبه الحديث» when he reported a lie and said the opposite of what was the case; but if it is doubled [with shadda] it is limited to one object." I did not find in the lexical books I have at hand anything that supports this; as for «كذبه الحديث», «الحديث» is accusative by removal of the preposition, on the sounder view. It is also permissible that «ما» be a maṣdar, and with what follows it be in the position of the accusative as the object of «كذب»; the meaning is that the heart did not make him imagine that he had seen when he had not seen, but rather the heart confirmed his sight.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «ثم دنا فتدلى» there is the art of inversion («القلب»), which is of the "inverted" («المقلوب») in which what is made clear by being later is put first, and what is made clear by being put first is put later; i.e. «تدلى فدنا» ("he hung down and so drew near"), because he hung down in order to draw near, and drew near by hanging down.
2- In His words «فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى» there is the art of vagueness («الإبهام»), which has been discussed before. It is frequent and common in the Qur'an, as if it were too great for explanation to encompass; so He left vague the matter He revealed to His servant and made it general, and this is more eloquent because the hearer's imagination goes in every direction regarding it. Fine is the saying of Durayd ibn al-Ṣimma:
صبا ما صبا حتى علا الشيب رأسه ... فلما علاه قال للباطل أبعد
(He was inclined, however he was inclined, until grey hair rose over his head; and when it rose over it, he said to falsehood, "Begone.")
and the saying of Abū Nuwās:
ولقد نهزت مع الغواة بدلوهم ... وأسمت سرح اللحظ حين أساموا
وبلغت ما بلغ امرؤ بشبابه ... فإذا عصارة كل ذلك أثام
(I surely took my turn with the misguided at their bucket, and I let my glance graze when they let theirs graze; and I attained what a man attains in his youth, and the sum total of all that was sin.)
His saying «وبلغت ما بلغ امرؤ بشبابه» is among the rare and elegant; and like it is the saying of another describing wine:
مضى بها ما مضى من عقل شاربها ... وفي الزجاجة باق يطلب الباقي
(What went of its drinker's reason went with it, and in the flask what remains seeks what remains.)
3- In «والنجم» to His words «وأدنى» there is an enchanting, captivating rhythm in a wondrous verbal cadence, depicting a majestic subject with miraculous mastery. The noble verse began with the oath by the star, which some Arabs used to put in the place of a deity; but the oath is not by the alleged deity alone, rather by it when it «falls» and drops from its heights, which deceived some simpletons and the weak-minded so that they made of it a god other than Allah; this fall wounds divinity, and the Noble Qur'an brought it with the oath as a completion of it, because it has extraordinary dimensions of meaning. Then the noble verse denied of the Arab Messenger the attribute of straying with which the deniers accused him, those whose straying reached the point that they worshipped the star, which has no immunity against falling. The verse stated in declaring the Qur'an, which was sent down upon the trustworthy Messenger, free of desire and emotion, and said of it that it is a revelation from Allah, the Creator, the Strong, who commanded the Messenger to carry the message of the Qur'an, so he proclaimed the command and rose to give his people glad tidings of its guidance and to warn them regarding their denial of its right direction. This revelation was not one that invited doubt or casting doubt, but occurred while the noble Messenger was as near to his Lord, Glorified and Exalted, as can be: that he was at a distance of the space between the two ends of the bow, and the Arabs know the shortness of the distance between them with full knowledge, because the bow lives in their hands and accompanies them all the time.

dervis-irab:12-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَفَتُمارُونَهُ) From «المماراة» and «المراء», i.e. quarrelling and disputing. It is derived from «مرى الناقة» (milking the she-camel), as if each of the two disputants draws out («يمري») what the other has.
(سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهى) A lote tree at the farthest limit of Paradise to which the spirits of the martyrs resort. There is disagreement on the reason for its being so named, in eight views, the detail of which is in the longer works.

* I'rab:
(أَفَتُمارُونَهُ عَلى ما يَرى) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; «تمارونه» is a verb, agent and direct object; «على ما يرى» is attached to «تمارونه». By right it should have been made transitive with «في», as you say «جادلته في كذا», but it was made to include the sense of overcoming, so it was made transitive as that is. The clause «يرى» is the ṣila of the relative noun; it is also permissible that «ما» be a maṣdar.
(وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرى) The «واو» is circumstantial; the «لام» is for the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «رآه» is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. «نزلة» may be parsed as an adverbial of time, i.e. «مرة أخرى» ("another time"), because the maṣdar «النزلة» stands in the position of «المرة» of it; it may be parsed as a ḥāl, accusative with the accusative of a maṣdar that occupies the place of a ḥāl; and it may be parsed as an absolute object, as a confirming maṣdar. To that went Abū al-Baqāʾ, who implied «مرة أخرى» or «رؤية أخرى» ("another sight"). To the first went al-Zamakhsharī. Abū Ḥayyān allowed the three views and did not choose between them. «أخرى» is an adjective of «نزلة».
(عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهى) The adverbial is attached to «رآه», or is a ḥāl of the agent, or of the object, or of both together. «سدرة» is muḍāf ilayhi and «المنتهى» is annexed to «سدرة».
(عِنْدَها جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوى) The adverbial is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «جنة المأوى» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is a ḥāl of «سدرة المنتهى».
(إِذْ يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ ما يَغْشى) The adverbial is attached to «رآه»; the clause «يغشى السدرة» is in the position of the genitive through the adverbial's being annexed to it; «السدرة» is the direct object; «ما» is a relative noun, the agent of «يغشى»; and in it is the vagueness mentioned before.
(ما زاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَما طَغى) «ما» is negative; «زاغ البصر», its verb is past, with an agent; «وما طغى» is conjoined to «ما زاغ», i.e. his sight did not incline away from what it saw, nor did it exceed it, that night.
(لَقَدْ رَأى مِنْ آياتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرى) The «لام» is for the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «رأى» is a past verb, its agent a latent pronoun; «من آيات ربه» is a ḥāl fronted before the object; «الكبرى» is the object of «رأى». The implied form is: "He indeed saw the greatest signs, as being part of the signs of his Lord." It is possible that «الكبرى» is an adjective of «آيات ربه» and not a direct object, and the thing seen is omitted, to magnify and glorify the matter, as if He had said: "He indeed saw of the greatest signs of his Lord mighty things that description cannot encompass." Omission in a case like this is more eloquent and awe-inspiring, because it magnifies the greatest signs of Allah, and holds that among them is what he saw and what he did not see; whereas on the first view the requirement is that he saw all the greatest signs, comprehensively and generally, although the signs of Allah are such that no one can encompass them in their totality.

dervis-irab:19-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اللَّاتَ) The following is in al-Qāmūs: "«اللات» with a doubled «تاء» is an idol; Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima and a group read it so. It was named after the one at whose place «السويق» (barley meal) used to be mixed («يلتّ») with clarified butter; then it was lightened." In al-Baḥr [al-Muḥīṭ] are his words: "«واللات» is an idol which the Arabs venerated. Qatāda said it was at al-Ṭāʾif; Abū ʿUbayda and others said it was in the Kaʿba; Ibn Zayd said: it was at Nakhla near the market of ʿUkāẓ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said Qatāda's statement is the more likely, and it is supported by the poet's words:
وفرّت ثقيف إلى لاتها ... بمنقلب الخائب الخاسر
(Thaqīf fled to its Lāt, with the return of the disappointed, the loser.)
The «تاء» in «اللات» is said to be original, the lām of the word, like the «باء» in «باب», and its «ألف» is apparently converted from a «ياء», since the root «ليت» exists; if a root from «ل و ت» exists, it may be converted from a «واو». It is also said that the «تاء» is feminine and its pattern is «فَعْلة» from «لوى», it being said that they used to «bend» («يلوون») over it and devote themselves to worship, or «twist» around it, i.e. circumambulate it; its lām was omitted. The majority read «اللات» with a light «تاء»; Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ṭalḥa, Abū al-Jawzāʾ, Yaʿqūb and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read it with it doubled. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this was a man at the market of ʿUkāẓ who mixed clarified butter and barley meal at a rock."
(الْعُزَّى) The pattern «فُعْلى» from «العِزّ» (might); it is the feminine of «الأعزّ», like «الفضلى» and «الأفضل». It is the name of an idol; it is also said to have been a tree that was worshipped. The wording of al-Kashshāf: "«والعزى» belonged to Ghaṭafān, and it was a samura tree; its origin is the feminine of «الأعزّ». The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to it and he cut it down, and a she-devil came out of it with her hair loose, calling out, and her attendant striking her head with her hand. He kept striking her with the sword until he killed her, while she was saying:
يا عزّ كفرانك لا سبحانك ... إني رأيت الله قد أهانك
(O ʿUzzā, [we offer] your denial, not your glorification; I have seen that Allah has humiliated you.)
He returned and told the Messenger of Allah, who said, peace be upon him: that is al-ʿUzzā, and it will never be worshipped again." In al-Qāmūs: "«والعزى» is the mighty one, the feminine of «الأعزّ», an idol or a samura tree worshipped by Ghaṭafān. The first to take it was Ẓālim ibn Asʿad, above Dhāt ʿIrq toward al-Bustān at nine miles; he built a house over it and called it «بُسًّا», and they used to hear a voice in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to it, and he demolished the house and burned the samura."
(مَناةَ) A rock belonging to Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa; on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, to Thaqīf. Its derivation is from «مَنى يَمني», i.e. to pour out, because the blood of the sacrifices was poured out beside it.
(ضِيزى) Unjust, from «ضازه يضيزه» when he wronged him and was unjust to him. On this it admits two analyses. One is that it is an adjective on the pattern «فُعلى» with ḍamma on the first letter, and the first letter was given kasra so that the «ياء» would be sound, like «بِيض». If it is asked: what necessity calls for supposing that its original had ḍamma on the first letter, and why not say it is «فِعلى» with kasra? The answer is that Sībawayh related that no adjective on «فِعلى» with kasra on the first letter has occurred; only with ḍamma has it occurred, such as «حُبلى», «أُنثى», «رُبى» and the like. But someone else has related such adjectives: Thaʿlab related «ميتة حِيكى» and «رجل كِيسى», and another related «امرأة عِزهى» and «امرأة سِعلى». This does not refute Sībawayh, because Sībawayh says of «حيكى» and «كيسى» what he says of «ضيزى», namely that the «ياء» is made sound; as for «عزهى» and «سعلى», the well-known forms of them are «عزهاة» and «سعلاة». The second analysis is that it is a maṣdar like «ذكرى». Al-Kisāʾī said: one says «ضاز يضيز ضيزى» like «ذكر يذكر ذكرى». It was also read «ضِئزى» with a quiescent hamza; the meaning of «ضأزه يضأزه» is: he diminished him through wrong and injustice, and it is close to the former. In al-Mukhtār: "«ضاز في الحكم» means he was unjust; «ضازه فيه» means he diminished him and cheated him; their pattern is that of «باع»." More discussion of this word will come in the section on Rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّى وَمَناةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرى) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; the «فاء» is a conjunction, to order the seeing after what was mentioned of His affairs, the Exalted, which are contrary to it in the utmost degree. The implied sense is: "After what you have heard of the traces of His perfection and the carrying out of His command in the highest assembly and beneath the layers of the earth, have you considered these idols, with their utmost insignificance and feebleness, as partners of Allah, the Exalted?" «رأيتم» is a verb and agent; «اللات» is its object; «العزى» and «مناة» are conjoined to «اللات»; «الثالثة» and «الأخرى» are two adjectives, the first an adjective of the two before it, and the second a adjective of censure for «الثالثة». The secrets of these adjectives will come in the section on Rhetoric. The second object of «رأيتم» is omitted, its implied form being «قادرة على شيء» ("able to do anything"); and it may be from the seeing of the eye, so it needs no second object.
(أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنْثى) The hamza is also for rebuking interrogation; «لكم» is a fronted khabar and «الذكر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «وله الأنثى» is conjoined to «لكم الذكر».
(تِلْكَ إِذاً قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزى) «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ, the demonstrative referring to the division understood from the interrogative clause; «إذن» has the sense of reply and consequence, the meaning being "since you have made for Him daughters and for yourselves sons"; «قسمة» is the khabar and «ضيزى» is an adjective of «قسمة».
(إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْماءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوها أَنْتُمْ وَآباؤُكُمْ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِها مِنْ سُلْطانٍ) «إن» is negative; «هي» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «أسماء» is the khabar of «هي»; «سميتموها» is a verb, agent, and second object, the first being omitted, its implied form being «أصناما» ("idols"); «أنتم» is emphasis for the agent so that the conjoining of «وآباؤكم» to it is sound, according to the saying of the author of al-Khulāṣa:
وإن على ضمير رفع متصل ... عطفت فافصل بالضمير المنفصل
(If you conjoin to an attached nominative pronoun, then separate it with the detached pronoun.)
The clause «سميتموها» is an adjective of «أسماء», and likewise the clause «ما أنزل»; «ما» is negative; «أنزل الله» is a verb and agent; «بها» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «سلطان»; «من» is a redundant preposition; and «سلطان» is genitive in form and accusative in position as a direct object.
(إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَما تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ وَلَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمُ الْهُدى) «إن» is negative; «يتبعون» is a nominative imperfect verb by the persistence of the «نون», the «واو» being the agent; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «الظن» is the object of «يتبعون»; the «واو» is a conjunction; «ما» is a relative conjoined to «الظن», and you may make it a maṣdar particle. The «واو» is circumstantial or parenthetical; the «لام» is for the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «جاءهم» is a past verb with a fronted direct object; «من ربهم» is attached to «جاءهم»; «الهدى» is the agent of «جاءهم»; and the clause is either a ḥāl from the agent of «يتبعون» or parenthetical with no grammatical position. There is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the third person, as a turning away from them and belittling of their affair.
(أَمْ لِلْإِنْسانِ ما تَمَنَّى) «أم» is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿa), with the sense of «بل», and the hamza is for denial; «للإنسان» is a fronted khabar and «ما» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «تمنى» is the ṣila of «ما», i.e. that which he wished for and hoped for from the idols.
(فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولى) The «فاء» is a conjunction on an implied clause understood from the meaning of «أم», i.e. "the matter is not so"; «لله» is a fronted khabar, «الآخرة» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «الأولى» is conjoined to «الآخرة».

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «ومناة الثالثة الأخرى» are astonishing secrets that need much sharpness and precision to extract the captivating beauty they contain. He described Manāt with His words «الثالثة» because she is lower in rank than Allāt and al-ʿUzzā, being in their view beneath them in standing. As for the description by His words «الأخرى», it strengthens this meaning and adds to her baseness; otherwise He would have said «الأخريات». Al-Zamakhsharī noticed this subtle secret and said: "«والأخرى» is censure; she is the one who comes later, of low worth, as in His words «وقالت أخراهم لأولاهم», i.e. their lowly ones to their chiefs and nobles." This point leads us to an interesting investigation of «الأخرى». It is the feminine of «آخَر», and there is no doubt that it originally derives from existential lateness («التأخر الوجودي»). But the Arabs turned it from use for existential lateness to use where a different thing was mentioned earlier, nothing more, until they stripped it of its indication of the original meaning, unlike «آخِر» and «آخِرة» on the pattern of «فاعل» and «فاعلة», whose suggestion of existential lateness is established and unchanged. Hence they turned from saying «ربيع الأخر» on the pattern of «أفعل» and «جمادى الأخرى» to «الآخِر» on the pattern of «فاعل» and «جمادى الآخِرة» on the pattern of «فاعلة», because they wanted to convey existential lateness, since «أفعل» and «فُعلى» from this derivation are stripped of indication of their purpose, so they turned from them to «الآخر» and «الآخرة» and held to that for both.
2- In His words «تلك إذن قسمة ضيزى» there is also a wondrous art. The ignorant may ask about the secret in using the word «ضيزى», which is wild and unfamiliar. We shall give what Ibn al-Athīr gave in al-Mathal al-Sāʾir regarding it, then follow it with what we have extracted ourselves. Ibn al-Athīr said: "A philosophising man was present with me one day, and mention of the Noble Qur'an came up. I began to describe it and to mention the eloquence and rhetoric its words and meanings contain. That man said: 'What eloquence is there, when it says «تلك إذن قسمة ضيزى»? Is there in the word «ضيزى» any beauty to be described?' I said to him: Know that in the use of words there are secrets you have not come to know, neither you nor your imams such as Ibn Sīnā and al-Fārābī, nor those who led them astray such as Aristotle and Plato. This word that you denied in the Qur'an, namely «ضيزى», in its place no other word can fill its place. Do you not see that the entire sūra, which is Sūrat al-Najm, is rhymed on the letter «ياء», for He said: «والنجم إذا هوى، ما ضلّ صاحبكم وما غوى» and so on to the end of the sūra? When He mentioned the idols, the division of children and what the unbelievers used to claim, He said «ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى تلك إذن قسمة ضيزى». This word came on the rhyming letter on which the whole sūra came, and no other can fill its place in its position. And if we come down with you, O stubborn one, to what you want, we say: a word other than this is better than it, but in this place it would not come fitting with its sisters nor suitable, for it would be outside the letter of the sūra. I shall make that clear and say: if we bring a word with the meaning of this word, we say «قسمة جائرة» or «ظالمة», and there is no doubt that «جائرة» or «ظالمة» is better than «ضيزى»; but if we arrange the speech and say «ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى تلك إذن قسمة ظالمة», the arrangement would not be like the first arrangement, and the speech would become like something lacking that needs completion; and this is not hidden from one who has taste and knowledge of the arrangement of speech. When that man heard what I put to him, his tongue swelled in his mouth, silenced, and he had nothing in that but obstinacy."
This is what Ibn al-Athīr said; it is good and shows taste and understanding, but it does not go beyond verbal limits. We shall mention what occurred to the mind of a matter of meaning relating to this speech. We say: since the purpose was to disparage their statement, refute their division, and denounce it, a word was chosen for it suited to disparagement and denunciation, as if the baseness of the word pointed to the baseness of their understandings. And this is among the most wondrous that occurs in the Noble Qur'an of the agreement of words with the requirement of the situation.

dervis-irab:26-30.t:
* I'rab:
(وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّماواتِ) «والأرض» The «واو» is a conjunction; «كم» is the informative «كم» (kam khabariyya), in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «من ملك» is in the position of the accusative as the tamyīz (specification) of the informative «كم», its discussion having preceded; «في السموات والأرض» is an adjective of «ملك»; the clause «لا تغني شفاعتهم» is the khabar; and «شيئا» is the object of «تغني» or an absolute object, i.e. "anything of avail".
(لا تُغْنِي شَفاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئاً إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَرْضى) «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «من بعد» is attached to «تغني»; «أن» and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, genitive through annexation to «بعد»; «الله» is the agent of «يشاء»; and «يرضى» is conjoined to «يشاء».
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنْثى) «إن» and its noun; the clause «لا يؤمنون» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «بالآخرة» is attached to «يؤمنون»; the «لام» is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «يسمّون الملائكة» is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object, the clause being the khabar of «إن»; and «تسمية الأنثى» is an absolute object.
(وَما لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ) The «واو» is circumstantial; «ما» is negative; «لهم» is a fronted khabar; «من» is a redundant preposition; «علم» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
(إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئاً) «إن» is negative; «يظنون» [Translator's note: the source says «يظنون», although the verse has «يتبعون»] is a nominative imperfect verb by the persistence of the «نون», the «واو» being the agent; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «الظن» is the direct object; the «واو» is circumstantial; «إن» is a particle resembling the verb, «الظن» is its noun, and the clause «لا يغني» is its khabar; «من الحق» is attached to «يغني»; and «شيئا» is a direct object or an absolute object.
(فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْ مَنْ تَوَلَّى عَنْ ذِكْرِنا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا) The «فاء» is the eloquent «فاء»; «أعرض» is an imperative verb; «عمّن» is attached to «أعرض»; the clause «تولى عن ذكرنا» is the ṣila of «من», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تولى»; the «واو» is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «يرد» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «الحياة» is the direct object; and «الدنيا» is an adjective.
(ذلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ) «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ; the demonstrative refers to their eager rush toward this world and turning away from the remembrance of Allah. It is also said that «ذلك» refers to their making the angels daughters of Allah; and it is said to refer to conjecture, i.e. the utmost they do is take hold of conjecture. «مبلغهم» is the khabar; «من العلم» is attached to «مبلغهم»; and the clause is parenthetical between the command, which is «أعرض», and its coming reason; al-Zamakhsharī chose it, and Abū Ḥayyān said it is not apparent.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدى) «إن» and its noun; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعلم» the khabar; «بمن» is attached to «أعلم»; the clause «ضلّ عن سبيله» is a ṣila; the clause «هو أعلم» is the khabar of «إن»; and the clause «هو أعلم بمن اهتدى» is conjoined to the preceding clause.

* Benefits:
1- Know that «كم» is a singular masculine noun, set down for plurality, with which any counted thing is expressed, many or few, masculine and feminine alike. It thus has a meaning and a form, and in this it runs the course of «كل», «أيّ», «من» and «ما», in that each of them has a form and a meaning: its form is masculine singular, and in meaning it applies to the dual and the plural. The pronoun in the verse was made plural with regard to the meaning; had it been carried by the form, He would have said «شفاعته».
2- Among the innovations of al-Khaṭīb [al-Rāzī] in his great tafsīr is an interesting reason for His naming the angels with the naming of females. He said: "That is because they saw in «الملائكة» the feminine «تاء» and it was sound among them to say «سجدت الملائكة», so they said: the angels are daughters of Allah, and named them with the naming of females." Perhaps this is what al-Zamakhsharī meant, followed by al-Bayḍāwī, in their words: "because when they say that the angels are daughters of Allah, they have named each one of them a daughter."

dervis-irab:31-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اللَّمَمَ) Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is that a person does something at a moment and it is not a habit of his; from it comes «إلمام الخيال» (the visit of the phantom), and «الإلمام» is a surplus that does not extend, and likewise «اللمام». Umayya said:
إن تغفر اللهمّ تغفر جما ... وأيّ عبد لك لا ألمّا
(If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive abundantly; and which servant of Yours has not committed a lapse?)
It has been reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite them and say them, meaning he did not commit a sin. And Aʿshā of Bāhila said:
تكفيه خرة فلذ إن ألمّ بها ... من الشواء ويروي شربه الغمر"
(A chunk of roast, if he partakes of it, suffices him, and a small drink quenches his thirst.)
On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: "«اللمم» is the glance, the wink and the kiss." On the authority of al-Suddī: "the passing thought of a sin." On the authority of al-Kalbī: "every sin for which Allah did not mention a prescribed punishment nor torment." On the authority of ʿAṭāʾ: "the habit of the soul from time to time." Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad said: "The origin of «اللمم» is that one comes near something without committing it; one says «ألمّ بكذا» when he approached it without mixing with it." Al-Azharī said: "The Arabs use «الإلمام» in the sense of nearness and proximity." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«واللمم» with two fatḥas is approaching a sin; it is also said to be the minor sins; it is also said to be doing a minor sin and then not repeating it. «لمّ بالشيء يلمّ» is of the pattern «ردّ»."
Among the strange things about the «لام» and the «ميم», when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, is that they indicate the sense of a quick glimpse and a swift, gentle passing. Among that: «ألمأ اللص على الشيء» (the thief swooped on the thing): he went off with it; «وما ذقت لماجا» with fatḥa on the «لام»: I tasted nothing that one smacks the lips over, i.e. savours; «لمح البرق والنجم»: it flashed from afar, and «برق لمّاح»; «ولمحته ببصري ورأيته لمحة البرق» and it is faster than «لمح البصر» (the glance of the eye); «اللمس» (touching) is well known and in it is the sense of stealing; and figuratively «لامس المرأة» and «لمسها» means he had intercourse with her, and it is not hidden what these suggest of stealth, seizing opportunity and keeping from sight. «لمظ الرجل يلمظ وتلمظ» when he follows with his tongue the remnant of food after eating, or wipes his lips with it, and the name of that remnant is «اللماظة»; «شرب الماء لماظا» with kasra: he tasted it with the tip of his tongue; and figuratively «تلمظت الحية» the snake put out its tongue, and «تلمظ بذكره»: he relished mentioning him. A man of Banū Ḥanīfa said:
فدع عربيا لا تلمظ بذكره ... فألأم منه حين ينسب عائبه
لقد كان متلافا وصاحب نجدة ... ومرتفعا عن جفن عينيه حاجبه
(Leave an Arab; do not relish mentioning him, for his fault-finder is meaner than he when lineage is traced. He was a squanderer, a man of courage, with his eyebrow raised above the lid of his eye.)
i.e. he did not commit a disgrace for which he would lower his gaze. And "this world is nothing but a «لماظة» of days". And he said:
وما زالت الدنيا يخون نعيمها ... وتصبح بالأمر العظيم تمخض
لماظة أيام كأحلام نائم ... يذعذع من لذّاتها المتبرض
(The world's delight has ever been treacherous, and each morning it labours with some great matter; a morsel of days like the dreams of a sleeper, from whose pleasures the one who takes little is scattered.)
i.e. the one who makes do with little. «لمع البرق والصبح وغيرهما لمعا ولمعانا» (lightning and dawn and the like flashed) and «برق لامع» and «لمّاع», and «بروق لمع ولوامع». Among their sayings: «أخدع من يلمع» (more deceptive than the one that gleams), which is a lightning without rain, and the mirage; «فلاة لمّاعة» a wasteland that glints with mirage; «به لمعة ولمع» of blackness or whiteness or any colour; «ثوب ملمّع» a garment variegated, «لمّعه ناسجه» its weaver variegated it, and in it are «تلميع» and «تلاميع» when it has various colours. Labīd ibn Rabīʿa said: "«إن استه من برص ملمّعه»" (his rump is variegated with leprosy). «رجل ألمعي ويلمعي» a shrewd man. Figuratively «لمع الزمام» (the rein flashed): it flapped with a gleam; «زمام لامع ولموع». Dhū al-Rumma said:
فعاجا علندى ناجيا ذا براية ... وعوّجت مذعانا لموعا زمامها
(They turned a stout, swift she-camel with a nose ring, and turned a docile one whose rein gleamed.)
«والطائر يلمع بجناحيه» the bird flaps its wings, and «خفق بملمعيه» with its wings; «لمع بثوبه ويده وسيفه» he signalled with his garment, hand and sword; «وما بالدار لامع» there is no one in the house; «وأصاب لمعة من الكلأ» he got a little pasturage; «ومعه لمعة من العيش» some sustenance with which one gets by. ʿAdī said:
تكذب النفوس لمعتها ... وتعود بعد آثارا
(Souls belie their glimmer and afterwards return as traces.)
i.e. life departs from them and returns as traces and tales. A Bedouin mentioned a tax collector and said: «فلمقه بعد ما نمقه» i.e. he erased it after he had written it. «وما ذقت لماقا» I tasted nothing. «وامرأة لمياء بيّنة اللّمى» a woman with evident «لمى», which is the dark colour in the inside of the lip; and figuratively «رمح ألمى» a dark spear, «قناة لمياء», «ظل ألمى» dense, dark shade, «شجر ألمى الظلال» and «شجرة لمياء الظل»:
إلى شجر ألمى الظلال كأنه ... رواهب أحر من الشراب عذوب
(Toward trees of dark shade, as if they were nuns, fresh from drinking, sweet.)
[Translator's note: the last verse is translated as it stands in the source, whose wording is unclear.]
(أَجِنَّةٌ) The plural of «جنين» (foetus). It was named «جنين» because of its being concealed in its mother's womb. The discussion of this root and what it indicates has already preceded.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The «واو» is resumptive; «لله» is a fronted khabar; «ما» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; «في السموات» is the ṣila of «ما»; «وما في الأرض» is conjoined to «ما في السموات»; and the clause is a resumption, driven to inform of the perfection of His power.
(لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَساؤُا بِما عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَى) The «لام» is the lām of consequence or of becoming, and it is not for giving a reason, meaning that the outcome of the affair of creation is that among them there is the doer of good and the doer of evil; so for the doer of evil is the worse, and for the doer of good is the best. It is attached to what the meaning of dominion indicates. «يجزي» is an imperfect verb, subjunctive through an implied «أن» after the lām of consequence. It is also said that it has the sense of giving a reason, and the clarification of this meaning is that the reason is for misleading whom He wills and guiding whom He wills. «الذين» is a direct object; the clause «أساءوا» is the ṣila of «الذين»; «بما عملوا» is attached to «يجزي»; and «الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى» is conjoined to what preceded.
(الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَواحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ) «الذين» is in the position of the accusative as a badal of «الذين», or in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who avoid"; the clause «يجتنبون» is the ṣila of «الذين»; «كبائر الإثم» is the object of «يجتنبون»; «الفواحش» is conjoined to «كبائر الإثم»; «إلا» is a particle of exception; «اللمم» is excepted with «إلا», and it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because there is nothing before it within which it is included; it may be a continuous one according to whoever explains «اللمم» as other than minor sins. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be of the type «لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله», in which case «إلا» has the sense of «غير» and is an adjective of «كبائر الإثم», its i'rab appearing in what follows it.
(إِنَّ رَبَّكَ واسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ) «إن» and its noun; «واسع المغفرة» is its khabar; and the clause gives a reason for the exception of «اللمم» and has no grammatical position.
(هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ) «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعلم» the khabar; «بكم» is attached to «أعلم»; «إذ» is an adverbial for past time, also attached to «أعلم»; the clause «أنشأكم» is in the position of the genitive through the adverbial's being annexed to it; «من الأرض» is attached to «أنشأكم»; «إذ» is conjoined to the first «إذ»; «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ and «أجنّة» its khabar; and «في بطون أمهاتكم» is an adjective of «أجنّة».
(فَلا تُزَكُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقى) The «فاء» is the eloquent «فاء»; «لا» is prohibitive; «تزكوا» is an imperfect verb made jussive by the prohibitive «لا», its sign of jussive being the dropping of the «نون», the «واو» being the agent; «أنفسكم» is the direct object; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعلم» the khabar; «بمن اتقى» is attached to «أعلم»; and the clause «اتقى» is the ṣila of the relative noun.

dervis-irab:33-62.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَوَلَّى) «تولّى عنه»: he turned away from it and left it; «تولّى هاربا»: he turned his back. More of its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(أَكْدى) He withheld his giving and cut it off. Its origin is «إكداء الحافر» (the digger's coming up against hard ground), which is that he meets a «كُدية», a hardness like a rock, and so stops digging. More of its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(أَقْنى) He gave wealth that is taken as a possession. «القنية» is wealth that you have amassed and resolved should not leave your hand. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "«قني الرجل يقنى قنى» like «غني يغنى غنى», then it becomes transitive by changing the vowel, so one says «قنيت له مالا» (I earned wealth for him), like «شترت عين الرجل» and «شترها الله»." Al-Rāghib said: the reality is that He made wealth a possession for him; and «قنيت كذا» and «أقنيته».
(الشِّعْرى) There are two «الشعريان», i.e. two stars; one of them is called «الشعرى العبور», and that is what is meant in the Noble Verse, for Khuzāʿa used to worship it. Abū Kabsha, a man of their chiefs, instituted its worship. He said: because the stars cross the sky breadthwise and al-Shiʿrā crosses it lengthwise, it differs from them; so he worshipped it, and Khuzāʿa and Ḥimyar worshipped it. Abū Kabsha was one of the Prophet's ﷺ forefathers on his mothers' side, and for that reason the polytheists of Quraysh used to call the Prophet ﷺ "the son of Abū Kabsha" when he called to Allah the Exalted and opposed their religions, likening him to that man in that he had innovated a religion other than theirs. It rises after Gemini in the intensity of the heat and is called «الشعرى اليمانية». The second is «الشعرى الغميصاء», from «الغمص» with two fatḥas, which is the flowing of tears from the eye.
(الْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ) The overturned one, which is the one whose upper part became its lower and whose lower became its upper.
(أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُ) i.e. the near one drew near. Al-Nābigha said:
أزف الترحل غير أن ركابنا ... لما تزل برحالنا وكأن قد
(The departure has drawn near, except that our riding camels have not yet moved off with our saddles — and as though they had.)
And Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
بان الشباب وأمسى الشيب قد أزفا ... ولا أرى لشباب ذاهب خلفا
(Youth has departed and grey hair has drawn near, and I see no replacement for departed youth.)
In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«أزف الرحيل أزفا» of the pattern «تعب», and «أزفا» also: it drew near and approached; «أزفت الأزفة»: the Resurrection drew near."
(سامِدُونَ) «السمود» is heedless play; it is also said to be turning away; it is also said to be arrogance. Abū ʿUbayda said: «السمود» is singing in the language of Ḥimyar; they say: «يا جارية اسمدي لنا» i.e. sing for us. Al-Rāghib said: "«السامد» is the one at play who raises his head, from their saying «بعير سامد في مسيره»; it is also said «سمد رأسه وجسده» i.e. he shaved off his hair." In al-Mukhtār: "«السامد» is the one at play, and its pattern is that of «دخل»." Al-Zamakhsharī explained «السمود» as «البرطمة», a vernacular word that is also classical; in al-Ṣiḥāḥ «البرطمة» is swelling up with anger.

* I'rab:
(أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّى) The hamza is for affirmative interrogation; the «فاء» is a conjunction on an implied omitted clause; «رأيت» is a verb and agent, with the sense of «أخبرني» ("tell me"); «الذي» is the first object of «رأيت»; and the clause «تولى» is the ṣila.
(وَأَعْطى قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدى) The «واو» is a conjunction; «أعطى» is conjoined to «تولى»; «قليلا» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and you may make it a direct object; «أكدى» is conjoined to «أعطى».
(أَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرى) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; «عنده» is an adverbial attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «علم الغيب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a second object of «رأيت»; the «فاء» is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يرى» its khabar; and the clause is conjoined to the clause «أعنده علم الغيب», so it comes within the scope of the interrogation.
(أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِما فِي صُحُفِ مُوسى) «أم» is discontinuous, with the sense of «بل»; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «ينبأ» is an imperfect verb made jussive by «لم», its deputy agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; «بما» is in the position of the accusative as a second object of «ينبأ»; and «في صحف موسى» is attached to an omitted ṣila of «ما».
(وَإِبْراهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّى) «إبراهيم» is conjoined to «موسى»; «الذي» is an adjective; «وفى» is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(أَلَّا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى) «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لا تزر» is its khabar; «وازرة» is the agent of «تزر»; «وزر أخرى» is the object of «تزر»; and «أن» with what is in its scope is a badal of «ما في صحف موسى», so it is in the position of the genitive; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is that no bearer will bear...", so it would be in the position of the nominative.
(وَأَنْ لَيْسَ لِلْإِنْسانِ إِلَّا ما سَعى) «وأن» is conjoined to «أن لا تزر», so it is lightened like it; the clause «ليس» is its khabar; «للإنسان» is a fronted khabar of «ليس»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «ما» is a maṣdar particle; «سعى» is a verb; and the interpreted maṣdar is the noun of «ليس».
(وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرى) Conjoined to what preceded; «سعيه» is the noun of «أن» and the clause «سوف يرى» is the khabar of «أن».
(ثُمَّ يُجْزاهُ الْجَزاءَ الْأَوْفى) «ثم» is a conjunction; «يجزاه» is a passive imperfect verb, its deputy agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; the «هاء» is accusative by removal of the preposition, or it is a second object (one says «جزيته سعيه» and «بسعيه»); «الجزاء» is an absolute object; «الأوفى» is an adjective. The nominative pronoun refers to «الإنسان» and the accusative refers to «الجزاء». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "His words «الجزاء الأوفى» are the object of «يجزى» and not a maṣdar, because it is described by «الأوفى», and that is of the description of what is recompensed with, not of the description of the act." His statement is not far-fetched, and in that case it becomes necessary that the accusative pronoun be accusative by removal of the preposition; though that does not prevent a maṣdar's being described and remaining a maṣdar, since the act may be so described for emphasis. It is also permissible that the accusative pronoun be for «الجزاء», then be explained by His words «الجزاء الأوفى», so it is a badal of it or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
(وَأَنَّ إِلى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهى) Conjoined to what preceded; «إلى ربك» is the fronted khabar of «أن» and «المنتهى» is the postponed noun of «أن».
(وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكى) Also conjoined; «أن» and its noun; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, the clause «أضحك» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أن». «هو» may also be parsed as emphasis (tawkīd) for the noun of «أن». Some said it is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and the clause «أضحك» is the khabar of «أن»; most favoured it. They said: "In His words, the Exalted, «وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى وأنه هو أمات وأحيا وأنه خلق الزوجين الذكر والأنثى», the separating pronoun was brought in the first two but not the third, because some of the ignorant may ascribe these acts to other than Allah the Exalted, as the saying of Nimrod «أنا أحيي وأميت» (I give life and cause death); but as for the third, no one among people has claimed it."
(وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَماتَ وَأَحْيا) Conjoined to the previous verse, like it in its i'rab.
(وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى) The clause «خلق» is the khabar of «أن»; «الزوجين» is the direct object; «الذكر» is a badal of «الزوجين»; and «الأنثى» is conjoined to «الذكر».
(مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إِذا تُمْنى) «من نطفة» is attached to «خلق»; «إذا» is an adverbial for what is yet to come of time, governing its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; and the clause «تمنى» is in the position of the genitive through the adverbial's being annexed to it.
(وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرى) The verse is conjoined to what is before it; «عليه» is the fronted khabar of «أن» and «النشأة» its postponed noun; «الأخرى» is an adjective of «النشأة».
(وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنى وَأَقْنى) Conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab has already gone before.
(وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرى) Also conjoined.
(وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عاداً الْأُولى) «أن» and its noun; the clause «أهلك» is its khabar; «عادا» is the object of «أهلك»; «الأولى» is an adjective.
(وَثَمُودَ فَما أَبْقى) Conjoined to «عاد»; the «فاء» is a conjunction; «ما أبقى» is conjoined to «أهلك». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«وثمودا» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. «وأهلك ثمودا»; it cannot be a fronted object of «أبقى», because «ما» the negative has the right to the beginning of the clause, so what follows it does not operate on what is before it."
(وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغى) «وقوم نوح» is conjoined to «ثمود»; «من قبل» is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «قبل» is indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, not in meaning; «إن» and its noun; the ṣila «كانوا» [Translator's note: the source says «وصلة كانوا خبرها», literally "the ṣila of «كانوا» is its khabar", which appears to mean the clause «كانوا…» is the khabar of «إن»]; «كان» and its noun; «هم» is a separating pronoun with no grammatical position, and it may be emphasis for the pronoun in «كانوا»; «أظلم» is the khabar of «كانوا»; and «أطغى» is conjoined to «أظلم».
(وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوى) The «واو» is a conjunction; «المؤتفكة» is a fronted object of «أهوى», so the clause is conjoined; and you may conjoin «المؤتفكة» to what is before it.
(فَغَشَّاها ما غَشَّى) The «فاء» is a conjunction; «غشاها» is a verb with a latent agent; «ما» is a relative, the second object of «غشّى»; and the clause «غشّى» is a ṣila. It is possible that the doubled «غشّى» has the meaning of the simple verb, so that it takes one object and the agent is «ما», as in His words, the Exalted: «فغشيهم من اليمّ ما غشيهم».
(فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمارى) The «فاء» is the eloquent «فاء», i.e. "if you have known all this, then which of the favours of your Lord do you doubt?"; the «باء» is locative; the address is to the hearer; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تتمارى», i.e. you are in doubt; and it is a rebuking interrogation. The word «الآلاء» is applied to both favours and punishments, and these are favours about which no hearer should doubt, given what is in the punishments of rebuke and admonition for whoever takes heed and reflects.
(هذا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولى) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, referring to the Qur'an or to the Messenger ﷺ; «نذير» is the khabar and its tanwīn is for magnification; «من النذر» is an adjective of «نذير»; «النذر» is either the plural of an active participle, if we consider «نذير» an irregular active participle, or of a maṣdar, if we consider «نذير» an irregular maṣdar, since it is from «أنذر», whose regular active participle is «منذِر» and whose regular maṣdar is «مُنذَر» [Translator's note: as written in the source]; «الأولى» is an adjective of «النذر».
(أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُ) A verb and agent, i.e. the one described by nearness drew near, which is the Day of Resurrection.
(لَيْسَ لَها مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ كاشِفَةٌ) The clause is a ḥāl of «الآزفة»; «ليس» is a defective past verb; «لها» is a fronted khabar; «من دون الله» is a ḥāl; and «كاشفة» is the noun of «ليس». It may be a description or a maṣdar. If it is a description, the «تاء» in it is feminine, because it is then an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. «نفس كاشفة» or «حال كاشفة»; and the «تاء» in it may be for emphasis, like «علّامة» and «نسّابة»; and it may be a maṣdar, as al-Rummānī and his group said, like «العاقبة» and «خائنة الأعين».
(أَفَمِنْ هذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; the «فاء» is resumptive; «من هذا» is attached to «تعجبون»; «الحديث» is a badal of the demonstrative; «تعجبون» is a nominative imperfect verb. Wonder may be for denial, and may be for approval and acceptance; the first is what is intended by the rebuke.
(وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلا تَبْكُونَ) Conjoined to «تعجبون».
(وَأَنْتُمْ سامِدُونَ) The «واو» is circumstantial or resumptive; «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ and «سامدون» its khabar; the clause is either circumstantial or resumptive.
(فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا) The «فاء» is the eloquent «فاء», i.e. "if you have reflected on all this and grasped it as it should be grasped, then prostrate"; «اسجدوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the «نون»; «لله» is attached to «اسجدوا»; «اعبدوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «فاسجدوا», and the direct object is omitted.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «أفرأيت الذي تولى» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because He borrowed turning the back and turning away for not entering into belief. This can serve as a rule for the mention of «التولي» in the Qur'an: wherever it occurs absolute, unqualified, its meaning is non-belief. And in His words «وأعطى قليلا وأكدى» there is an explicit metaphor: the one who gives a little and then withholds giving is likened to the one who «يكدي», i.e. stops digging after something hard as a rock stands in the way of it. Imam al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt: "«الكدية» is the hardness of the ground; one says «حفر فأكدى», and that was borrowed for the importunate seeker and the scanty giver, as the Exalted said: «أعطى قليلا وأكدى»."
2- In His words «أضحك وأبكى», «أمات وأحيا», «أعطى وأكدى» and «الذكر والأنثى» there is an antithesis (ṭibāq) that is not hidden, and it is multiple in the whole sūra, and for this reason it falls under the chapter of contrast (muqābala). This antithesis is increased in beauty by its coming in the setting of fluent rhyme, because of the complete correspondence in the verse endings.
3- In His words «وأنه هو رب الشعرى» there is the art of pointed specification (tankīt), which is that the speaker aims at mentioning one thing to the exclusion of another that would fill its place, for a point in the thing mentioned that favours its mention over any other. Allah, Glorified, singled out al-Shiʿrā for mention among the stars, though He is Lord of everything, for what we mentioned in the section on Vocabulary: that a man known as Abū Kabsha, "servant of al-Shiʿrā", appeared among the Arabs and called to its worship, so Allah sent down the verse.
4- In His words «ليس لها من دون الله كاشفة» there is the art of proverbial illustration (tamthīl), for He brought the speech out in the form of a current proverb used for illustration in events.
